title: zone of the creative promise — libra ii
content:
this series is inspired by my collaboration with LJ of Ceremony for their communal writing practice, Atmospheres, based of the 36 decans of the astrological year.

Libra II — 4 October – 13 October
Key themes from LJ — Bonds, Promises, Endurance
Before this: Initiation of the Artist Warrior Monk, Libra I

*

with the second decan of Libra — named by LJ as “Zone Rites” — I’ve been thinking about the sacred zone space that a promise creates, in any relationship.

a promise is binding, in that a promise activates an electric energy between two or more entities — be that between two people, between different parts of myself, or between myself and a creative project/practice I am practicing devotion to.

here, devotion is the key word that comes back to me. to me, devotion is not about unwavering commitment, but deep grappling with. I am devoted because I show up with my whole self to question, not because I am perfectly compliant.

binding commitment as power

the biggest reframe I’ve experienced in working with Libra II is to see the Three of Swords card (which used to fill me with love anxiety and terror) as not that of heartbreak and grief, but of binding, commitment, and the power of choice. when we commit to one thing, there is always the grief of unlived possibilities.

at the same time, it occurs to me that perhaps choosing one thing — anything, really, with totality — IS an activation of power that paradoxically encompasses all possibility — in a way that not choosing at all doesn’t. to choose is to claim belonging to oneself. this is not to say that the choice cannot change. it can, and it always does, if not necessarily in form, but always in texture.

     

creative work as a promise to oneself

the nature of binding promises applies to human relationships, but right now, what I am most interested in is how the territory of promise manifests with my creative practice — or, more generally, with the creative life force energy in me that wants to be expressed, in practice.

what if: every project I worked on, or every creative practice that I have IS its own promise between myself and this life energy. as in: I promise to show up, even if I don’t feel like it. I promise to put my pen to paper, even if I don’t know what will come out. I promise to share my work into the void, as a way of honoring my devotion to being visible — not just my desire to be seen.

the zone as sacred container

in reflecting on Libra II: Zone Rites with LJ, I’ve been inspired to see every creative practice I do — and every project I enter — as its own sacred zone space, with its own rules, logic, energy field, and texture.

the zone of making a podcast is very different than that of an illustration, or the zone of writing a book project. the zone of creating for Labyrinth is unlike any other course that I’ve taught. each project and practice activates different energies and impulses in me.

to create distinct boundaries for each zone — through ritual, process, and intention — IS what allows me to keep them safe, and to hold space for whatever intense, extreme things that want to emerge, without it spilling into the rest of my life. it would allow me to be more uncompromisingly too-much — because I can trust in the zone to hold it.

 

*

drawing this decan was challenging, because I didn’t want to repeat the same visual pattern from Libra I of the circular moon portal, crossed by swords. I ended up layering the image with different cross-sectional containers — such that the result is a pure extremity and excess, held in space by the pierced heart. it holds both boundaried sharpness, intensity, a delicate intricacy, softness, and an aching sort of pain. Libra II can hold all of that, with grace.
